title: Implementation-evidence loop
summary: This intermediate resource explains why the requested correction is blocked and what evidence is needed before an editor can update the guide without rewriting unaffected material.
prerequisites: The previous citation and its current first-party replacement or revision record
Access to the catalogue used to check identifier uniqueness

sections.title: Can the guide be corrected now?
paragraphs: No. This is an intermediate-level resource, and the requested correction cannot be applied safely from the supplied material.

The cited record under review is content/resources/coding-agents/implementation-evidence-loop.json. It is recorded as having an unregistered publisher and as never having been verified. Whether that citation moved or passed a review deadline is UNKNOWN because no former URL, replacement URL, previous verification date, or revision history was supplied.

The claims and procedure steps affected by the source change are also UNKNOWN. They are omitted rather than reconstructed. Applying substantive changes without the existing resource and the changed first-party source would replace reviewable history with unsupported content.
sections.callout: Do not treat missing source evidence as evidence that the guide is wrong. Stop the correction until the baseline resource and source-change record are available.

sections.title: Procedure for completing the correction
paragraphs: Step 1: Obtain the exact current JSON object from the target path, pinned to the revision being corrected. Preserve its field order, metadata, sections, callouts, code objects, and source records. If the object or revision cannot be obtained, stop and request the pinned baseline instead of drafting a replacement.

Step 2: Obtain the old citation and the current first-party replacement, revision notice, or publication history. Determine whether the source moved, changed content, or exceeded its declared review cadence. If that evidence is unavailable, record the change type as UNKNOWN and do not alter substantive claims.

Step 3: Compare the two source states and identify each claim or procedure step affected by the documented change. If a proposed edit cannot be traced to that change, leave the existing material untouched. If the comparison does not establish an affected passage, escalate it for source review rather than including it in the correction.

Step 4: Update only the affected passages and source metadata. Retain the existing title, category, format, audience, prerequisites, cadence, tags, section structure, callouts, and code unless the source change specifically requires one of them to change. If catalogue uniqueness or schema conformance cannot be checked, do not commit the update and request an authoritative catalogue and schema validation.

Step 5: Parse the completed file as JSON before committing it. JSON.parse throws a SyntaxError when text does not conform to JSON grammar. If parsing fails, correct the reported syntax problem and repeat the parse before continuing.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: The expected evidence is a pinned copy of the prior resource, a directly accessible HTTPS first-party source or revision record, a written identification of what changed, a mapping from that change to the affected passages, and a minimal JSON diff containing only those corrections.

Verify the result by comparing the updated object with the pinned baseline and confirming that every changed substantive passage maps to the documented source change. Confirm that unaffected passages and metadata are byte-for-byte unchanged where no schema migration requires otherwise.

Verify that the file parses successfully as one JSON object, that its identifier matches the target filename, and that the identifier is absent elsewhere in the shared catalogue. Verify each source URL over HTTPS and record the actual check date. If any source, mapping, parse result, or uniqueness check is missing, do not publish; return the item for the missing evidence.
